title: Gait adaptability on a virtual reality-based treadmill during neurorehabilitation: Study on the reliability and sensitivity to change of the C-Gait test
summary: This study examines a test (C-Gait Test) on a special treadmill (C-Mill), which has been used in (neurological) rehabilitation for several years. It examines how reliably and accurately the C-Gait test measures the correct result and, accordingly, what change value in the test can be attributed to a real training effect that cannot have arisen by chance or due to measurement inaccuracies. The participants with either Parkinsons's disease, multiple sclerosis or stroke complete the test a total of three times at different intervals as part of their neurological rehabilitation.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Rehabilitation-justifying and confirmed diagnosis of multiple sclerosis, EDSS 2 - 4.5, Parkinson's disease, Hoehn & Yahr stage I - III, or stroke (ICD-10 I61 oder I63)
- Ability to walk for 20 minutes without aids
- Sufficient cognitive abilities (Montreal Cognitive Assessment, MoCA
    - For patients with multiple sclerosis ≥ 26 points
    - For patients with Parkinson's disease or stroke ≥ 22 points
- A score of > 50 on the Barthel Index
- Sufficient knowledge of German to understand and follow instructions
- The patient is capable of beeing informed and to provide informed consent
- Written consent to participate in the study
Exclusion criteria:
- Exclusion criteria according to the device description (>135kg body weight, >2m height, open wounds in the area of the C-Mill safety belt, severe cognitive, visual or auditory impairments [cannot follow instructions or tasks])
- Other neurological or psychiatric disorders that negatively affect the ability to provide information, test comprehension or test safety
- Insufficient resilience to perform the C-Gait
- Insufficient knowledge of German to follow instructions and tests
